subject: Renewal: term re-profile + staggered top-up + soft auto-renew opt-out
messages:
From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@brightline.ai>
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@brightline.ai, marco.dangelo@brightline.ai
Date: Fri, 26 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal conversation — term profile & invoicing options

Hi Ben,

Thanks for the call this morning. As we discussed, Brightline is interested in renewing for the next 24 months but we'd like to change the shape of the contract to better match our usage profile: a low starting footprint (months 1–6), a planned ramp (months 7–12), and then a steady-state volume for year two.

A few asks from procurement:
- Can we spread the committed units across the 24 months (staggered top-up) to avoid big prepayments?
- We want a soft auto-renew opt-out clause (30 days) — we may migrate models after month 18 if strategic changes occur.
- For month-by-month overages during ramp, can we apply a small breakage credit rather than immediate penalty?

I attached a quick forecast. Can you propose a term structure + invoice cadence that keeps our per-token unit price predictable while reflecting this ramp?

Best,
Elena
Elena Rossi
Head of Platform Partnerships
Brightline HealthTech

Attachment: 2026-06-26-usage-forecast.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)
From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@brightline.ai>
Cc: priya_natarajan@redwood.ai, connor_obrien@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 26 Jun 2026 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation — term profile & invoicing options

Elena — thanks for the note and the forecast. High level response below; I pulled Priya (rev ops) and Connor (solutions) in to scope the mechanics.

Short answers:
1) Staggered top-up (phased committed units) — yes, we can structure a 24-month commit with ramped buckets. We typically map to 4 tranches (0–6, 7–12, 13–18, 19–24) and price each tranche with a blended effective rate.
2) Soft auto-renew opt-out — we can add a 30-day opt-out window before renewal; if exercised, the final month will move to usage-only and we prorate any remaining committed credits.
3) Overages during ramp — we can offer a 50% discount on overage rates for the first two months of any tranche while the KV cache and batching profile stabilizes (we call it a ramp grace credit).

Next steps I propose:
- I'll send a redline of the MAS with those clauses called out.
- Priya will run pricing scenarios against your forecast and propose three pricing shapes.
- Connor will confirm technical canary/burst behavior and whether we need a temporary dedicated pool at ramp start.

I attached a draft term sheet (redline) for quick review.

Regards,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachment: Brightline_MAS_v2_redline.pdf (pdf stub)
From: priya_natarajan@redwood.ai
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai, Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@brightline.ai>
Cc: connor_obrien@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 08:42:00 -0700
Subject: FW: Renewal conversation — pricing scenarios for Brightline

Hi Elena / Ben — attached are three pricing scenarios mapped to the forecast:
A) Conservative: small upfront commit, higher overage rate, evened invoice cadence (quarterly)
B) Balanced: staggered tranches with blended price (preferred)
C) Aggressive: larger commit early, lower unit price, up-front credit for excess usage

Key notes:
- For the staggered option we recommend quarterly invoice cadence with prorated first and last invoices. That avoids a single large initial cash flow.
- We propose a 6-month technical canary (1–2% reserved dedicated capacity) to mitigate cold-start and caching inefficiencies — billed at a nominal rate and applied as a credit to the first tranche.
- Option B includes the ramp grace credit Ben mentioned (50% off overage for two months after each tranche increase).

Please confirm which option you want modeled into a final amendment and whether procurement wants us to present a DocuSign for the redline.

Thanks,
Priya Natarajan
Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@brightline.ai>
To: priya_natarajan@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@brightline.ai, marco.dangelo@brightline.ai
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 10:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation — pricing scenarios for Brightline

Thanks Priya — Option B looks closest to what we want. A couple clarifications from procurement:
- Can the contract include a mid-term true-up window at month 12 with a 30-day notice trigger? We want a formal cadence for re-evaluating the committed tiers.
- For the soft auto-renew opt-out, procurement insists on an explicit migration assistance clause if they exercise the opt-out (30 days of reduced-ease-of-migration support + logs export assistance).

If you can add those two items to the amendment, we can route to legal. We'd like to avoid a single up-front prepay and prefer quarterly invoicing as you proposed.

Best,
Elena
From: connor_obrien@redwood.ai
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@brightline.ai>, ben_carter@redwood.ai, priya_natarajan@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 02 Jul 2026 09:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation — canary plan and migration assistance

Elena — quick note on the technical bits you asked for:
- Canary / temporary dedicated pool: we can reserve a small dedicated pool for the first 60 days of each tranche increase (not 6 months; we recommend 60 days unless you expect sustained spike). That reduces tail latency and cache warm-up penalty.
- Migration assistance (opt-out): we can commit to a 30-day migration support window that includes: exported request/response logs (7 days rolling by default, 30 days for migration), guidance doc for cache warming, and a discounted 1:1 engineer engagement rate for up to 10 hours.
- Instrumentation: we will enable per-route token-level cost tracking for the trial period so you can validate usage before the tranche fully takes effect.

If that works, Ben / Priya can fold the language into section 3 (term & billing) and section 9 (support & migration).

Cheers,
Connor O'Brien
Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference
From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@brightline.ai>
Cc: priya_natarajan@redwood.ai, connor_obrien@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 02 Jul 2026 15:08:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Renewal conversation — term re-profile; next steps

Elena — thanks for the quick turnaround. I updated the redline with two small edits:
- Added a month-12 true-up clause (30-day notice) with a mutually-agreed forecasting template.
- Clarified the opt-out migration assistance exactly as Connor outlined.

I also noted quarterly invoicing and the staggered tranche table; Priya attached the final pricing table in the redline. If you sign off, we'll send a DocuSign packet that:
1) Implements Option B (staggered tranches, blended rates)
2) Adds ramp grace credits for overages (50% discount for two months after each tranche increase)
3) Includes the 30-day soft auto-renew opt-out with migration assistance
4) Establishes a 60-day dedicated canary window at each tranche increase (Connor's recommendation)

If procurement is happy, please confirm and we'll route to legal + DocuSign today.

Warmly,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
